records.title: Proxy trust through app.trustProxy applied by the core on every adapter

acceptanceCriteria.text: Without `trustProxy(true)`, a request with `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `Forwarded: for=198.51.100.1;proto=https` from `127.0.0.1` has `req.remoteAddress()` `127.0.0.1` and `req.isSecure()` `false` on both the in-memory and the TinyHttpd adapter, so FR-HTTP-011 AC-2 (the default configuration) stays true. [D-080; FR-HTTP-011]

After `app.trustProxy(true)`, `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.1` gives `req.remoteAddress()` `203.0.113.7`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` gives `req.isSecure()` `true`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` gives `false`, and a request without these headers keeps the adapter's values. [D-080; D-225] Decision: trusted mode uses the left-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry and the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value, compared case-insensitively.

After `app.trustProxy(true)` the `Forwarded` header alone changes neither `remoteAddress()` nor `isSecure()`, and an empty or blank `X-Forwarded-For` entry keeps the adapter's remote address. [D-080] Decision: `Forwarded` is not interpreted in v1.

The trust decision is made in `DefaultRequest` from the app setting, so the in-memory adapter and the TinyHttpd adapter give identical `remoteAddress()` and `isSecure()` results for the same headers, and no adapter class reads `X-Forwarded-*` itself. [D-080; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter]

records.requirement: The system shall make `req.remoteAddress()` and `req.isSecure()` ignore `X-Forwarded-*` and `Forwarded` headers by default and, after `app.trustProxy(true)`, return the left-most address of the first `X-Forwarded-For` header and report a secure request when the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value is `https`, applied in the core's request object for every adapter.
records.rationale: Covers the proxy-trust API of D-225 for D-080 under the wave decision "Server settings reach the adapter" (proxy trust is not an adapter setting; the core applies it in `DefaultRequest` on every adapter, the in-memory one included). The trusted behaviour follows Express `app.set('trust proxy', true)`, which uses the left-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry and `X-Forwarded-Proto`; rejected alternative: a list of trusted proxy addresses (not in object.md; reopen if a deployment needs hop counting). The `Forwarded` header stays ignored even when trusted, as in Express.

records.title: Bootstrap AppFactory assembles TinyHttpd, Gson and the platform default logger for RestApp.create()

acceptanceCriteria.text: `DefaultAppFactory` is public with a public no-argument constructor, the `NaruServe` jar holds `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory` naming it, and in the `NaruServe` module test run `ServiceLoader.load(AppFactory.class, RestApp.class.getClassLoader())` finds exactly one provider and `RestApp.create()` returns a new app in state `NEW` on every call. [D-226; D-110; wave-4 carried: D-226 lookup with the real module] Decision: the provider class is `com.snoworca.naruserve.bootstrap.DefaultAppFactory`.

An app from `RestApp.create()` started with `listen(0)` answers a JSON echo route over a real socket: a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `{"name":"a"}` is decoded into a POJO through the default codec and sent back by `res.json`, and the app's internal adapter and codec are a `TinyHttpdAdapter` and a `GsonJsonCodec` built from `GsonJsonCodec.defaultGson()`. [D-228; D-110]

In the JVM test run, where `android.util.Log` is absent, `RestApp.create().logger()` is a `ConsoleLogger`; through a dedicated class loader that also sees a test-scope fake `android.util.Log`, the factory's app logger is a `LogcatLogger`. [D-402; D-169] Decision: the factory checks `Class.forName("android.util.Log", false, <its class loader>)` once per `create()` call.

The `NaruServe` jar holds `META-INF/proguard/naruserve-bootstrap.pro` with `-keep class com.snoworca.naruserve.bootstrap.DefaultAppFactory { public <init>(); }` and `-keepnames class com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory`, which a test reads from the built jar. [D-229] Decision: the file name is `naruserve-bootstrap.pro`.

`NaruServe-api` main classes still reference no TinyHttpd or Gson type (the build check of CON-BUILD-013), and the missing-module test of FR-APP-001 AC-3 keeps passing in the `NaruServe-api` test run. [D-226; D-227]

records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. records.title: Interim handler failure and unfinished-response handling

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with an empty body through the harness. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` but before commit is answered `500` with an empty body. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the `500` carries only `Content-Length: 0`; the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-8]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a wave 3 handler can reach) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; wave decision: abort() after completion; wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()` yields `202` with `X-A: 1` and an empty body, and the response is `COMPLETED`. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: when the handler returns with the response `NEW` the dispatcher calls `end()`, and with it `STREAMING` it runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-10]

[D-041; T01] Decision: `app.get(p, h)` and a builder `get(h)` record the same registration (method set `MethodSet.of(GET)`, pattern `p`, HTTP route kind), so the freeze reports such a pair as a duplicate. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-11]
Inside `h`, `req.method()` returns `Method.GET`, `Method.POST` and `Method.DELETE` for those three requests respectively. [D-042; T01]
After `app.route(Method.PATCH, "/p", h)`, `PATCH /p` reaches `h` with `req.method()` = `Method.PATCH`. [D-041; D-042]
`HEAD /users/1` reaches `h` through automatic `HEAD` with `req.method()` = `Method.HEAD`. [D-042; wave decision: req.method() during automatic HEAD]

records.title: Internal RestApp implementation with deferred router build and freeze

acceptanceCriteria.text: The implementation is a public class in a package documented as internal and not part of the API contract, it implements `RestApp`, and it holds the router and the dispatcher. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-393] Decision: the implementation is public class `DefaultRestApp` in package `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal`, whose package javadoc states it is not API. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-14]
A registration with an invalid pattern (one that `RoutePattern.parse` rejects) throws at the registration call itself, before any freeze. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-047; D-048]

`app.get("/a/b", h)` followed by `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build())` makes `GET /a//b` reach `h` after the harness freeze, showing the policy applies to registrations made before it. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; FR-ROUTE-006]

The `Router` is constructed only at the freeze, and a duplicate of D-044 surfaces as the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`, not at the second registration call. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-044] Decision: the freeze propagates the `RoutingConfigException` unchanged and leaves the app unfrozen, so `dispatcher()` keeps throwing `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-12]

After the harness freeze, `app.get(...)`, `app.route(Method, path, h)`, `app.route(MethodSet, path, h)` and `app.routerPolicy(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException`, and `RouteBuilder` registration methods (`get`, `put`, ...) throw `IllegalStateException` too, including on a builder obtained from `app.route(path)` before the freeze. [wave decision: Settings after the freeze] Decision: the internal WebSocket-route hook also throws `IllegalStateException` after the freeze, and a refused call records nothing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-13]
No public static method or constructor in package `com.snoworca.naruserve` returns a `RestApp` in wave 3. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-111]

The internal implementation (not the public `RestApp` interface) offers an internal WebSocket-route registration hook that records a WebSocket registration and passes it to `Router.addWebSocket` at the freeze; the test-fixtures harness uses it to register a WebSocket-only route, and wave 3 dispatches no handshake to that route (a matching upgrade request gets the same `426` as a plain `GET`) until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; wave decision: Working app in wave 3]

records.title: Request path, raw path and path parameter accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `GET /files/a%20b?x=1` matched by `/files/:name`, `req.path()` returns `/files/a b`. [D-073] Decision: `req.path()` percent-decodes the raw path once as UTF-8, keeps `+` as `+`, and applies no `mergeSlashes`, trailing-slash or case policy. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-1] Under `mergeSlashes(true)`, `GET /a//b` matched by `/a/b` gives `req.path()` = `/a//b` (the policy affects only route matching, not the decoded path). [wave 3 implementation decision]
For the same request `req.rawPath()` returns `/files/a%20b`, without `?x=1`. [D-074; wave decision: Remaining markers]
For the same request `req.param("name")` returns `a b`. [D-075]

`req.param("missing")` for a name not in the matched pattern throws an exception instead of returning `null`. [D-075] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException` and its message contains the name. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-2]

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-3]

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse throw `IllegalArgumentException`, which the dispatcher answers `400` with `Content-Length: 0` before the handler runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Header, remote address, secure flag and Last-Event-ID accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: With headers `X-Tag: a` and `x-tag: b`, `req.header("X-TAG")` returns `a`, `req.headers("x-Tag")` returns `[a, b]`, `req.header("None")` returns `null` and `req.headers("None")` returns an empty list. [D-079; T07] Decision: the empty list returned for no match is unmodifiable. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-5]

With the in-memory adapter reporting remote address `10.0.0.5` and secure `false`, a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `Forwarded: for=1.2.3.4;proto=https` still yields `req.remoteAddress()` = `10.0.0.5` and `req.isSecure()` = `false`. [D-080]

`req.lastEventId()` returns `42` for header `Last-Event-ID: 42` and `null` when the header is absent. [D-081] Decision: when `Last-Event-ID` appears more than once the first value is returned. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: Per-request concurrent attribute store

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `req.attribute("user", u)`, `req.attribute("user", User.class)` returns `u`, and `req.attribute("none", User.class)` returns `null`. [D-082]
An attribute stored while handling one request is not visible through `attribute(key, type)` of a second request, including two requests handled concurrently. [D-082]
Eight threads writing distinct keys to the same request's attributes concurrently leave every key readable with its value and no exception. [D-083]

With a typed `null` variable `Object v = null`, `req.attribute("k", v)` removes `k`, so a later `req.attribute("k", Object.class)` returns `null`; the value parameter is annotated `@Nullable`. [wave decision: Null attribute values; D-072]
`req.attribute("k", Integer.class)` with a stored `String` throws `ClassCastException`. [wave decision: Remaining markers]

records.title: Response body writers send, html, stream and end

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.send("hé")` writes the UTF-8 bytes `68 C3 A9` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, and after `res.header("Content-Type", "text/csv")` it keeps `text/csv`. [D-091] Decision: a body writer adds its default `Content-Type` only when no `Content-Type` header is set, compared case-insensitively. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-2]

`res.html("

é

")` writes UTF-8 bytes with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. [D-092]

`res.send(new byte[]{0, (byte) 0xFF, 10})` writes exactly those three bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` when none was set, and keeps an explicitly set `Content-Type`. [D-093; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`res.stream(in, "application/pdf")` with a 1 MiB input writes all bytes in order with `Content-Type: application/pdf`, and a counting input stream shows that every `read(byte[], int, int)` call requests fewer bytes than the 1 MiB input. [D-094] Decision: the copy reads with an 8192-byte buffer and writes each chunk to the exchange output stream in order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-3]

`res.stream(...)` closes the input stream exactly once after a successful copy, after a read failure, and after `res.abort(...)` during the transfer, including when the handler already returned; the caller does not close it. [D-094; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: the single close is guarded by a compare-and-set. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-4]

`res.end()` completes the response with the status and headers set so far and no body. [D-095] Decision: on a non-bodyless response `end()` commits with `Content-Length: 0`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-6]

`res.stream(InputStream, contentType)` does not block until the copy ends: it commits the response and returns, the copy to the end of the stream runs after the handler returns, and the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends; a test whose handler returns right after `res.stream(...)` observes the call return before the input is read to its end. [D-094; D-103; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: `stream` sets `Content-Type` to the argument, commits with unknown length, enters `STREAMING` and returns; the dispatcher runs the copy on the adapter thread after the handler returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Response commit flag, abort and header CR/LF rejection

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.isCommitted()` is `false` before any body write and `true` after `res.send("x")` handed the status and headers to the in-memory adapter. [D-096] Decision: `abort` before any commit leaves `isCommitted()` `false`, sets `ABORTED` and aborts the exchange without writing a status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-8]
`res.abort(new IOException("x"))` during a `stream(...)` transfer makes the in-memory adapter report the connection closed abnormally and leaves the response state `ABORTED`. [D-097]

`res.abort(...)` on a response that is already `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` does nothing: no exception, the state is unchanged and the adapter sees no further close. [wave decision: abort() after completion]

`res.header("X\r\nY", "1")`, `res.header("X", "a\nb")` and `res.header("X", "a\rb")` each throw an exception and add no header. [D-098] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException`, the header list stays unchanged, and the response-state check runs first. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-7] Besides CR and LF, `res.header` also throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a name that is not an RFC 9110 token (empty, or a char outside tchar) and for a value holding any control character other than HTAB (such as NUL or DEL) or any char above U+00FF. [wave 3 implementation decision]

records.title: Response state machine with single commit

acceptanceCriteria.text: A response starts in `NEW`, is `COMMITTED` once status and headers are handed to the adapter, and reaches `COMPLETED` after `send`; the adapter receives the status line and headers exactly once. [D-099]

`res.status(500)` or `res.header("X", "1")` after `res.send("a")` committed the response throws an exception and the sent status and headers stay unchanged. [D-100] Decision: the exception is `IllegalStateException` naming the current state, thrown in `COMMITTED`, `STREAMING`, `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED`, and nothing changes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-10]
A second body call (`send`, `html`, `stream` or `end`) after a body was sent throws an exception and writes no further bytes. [D-101]

After `res.stream(...)` returns, the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends, then `COMPLETED`, or `ABORTED` on abort; a read failure of the input stream during the copy, including after the handler returned, ends the response `ABORTED` with the input stream closed (FR-HTTP-014 AC-5). [D-103; D-097; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: a read failure during the copy sets `ABORTED`, calls `exchange.abort()` and closes the input, without rethrowing to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-11]

While the response is `STREAMING` (committed but not completed), `res.status(500)` and `res.header("X", "1")` each throw an exception and the status and headers the adapter received stay unchanged. [D-100; D-099]

records.title: Request body ownership with BodyState and BodyAlreadyConsumedException

acceptanceCriteria.text: `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` is a public class in `com.snoworca.naruserve` extending `RuntimeException`. [D-086; wave decision: Body ownership]

`BodyState` is an internal class whose state is `UNREAD` initially, `PARSING` while a reader holds the body, and `CONSUMED` after a completed read or `CLOSED` after the body was closed; a unit test drives each transition. [D-085] Decision: `close` moves to `CLOSED` from any state, and a later `begin` or shared parse throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-11]

A unit test acquiring the body through `BodyState` after a first read gets `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` when the second read is of a different kind (JSON, form/multipart or raw) or is a second JSON or raw read; the shared form/multipart parse of AC-4 is the only exemption. [D-086] Decision: `begin` in any state other than `UNREAD` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` naming the current state. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-9]

A unit test acquiring the shared form/multipart parse through `BodyState` repeatedly gets the same parse result each time without a second read of the stream and without `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [D-087] Decision: the shared parse after `begin`, or `begin` after the shared parse, throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`; a parser failure leaves `CONSUMED` with no cached result and later calls throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-10]
A reflection test finds no public body-reading method on `Request` at the wave 3 merge (wave 5 adds the body readers). [wave decision: Body ownership]

records.title: Limit-enforcing request body input stream

acceptanceCriteria.text: The stream is constructed from the source stream, a limit and an optional declared `Content-Length`; constructing it with limit `0` or a negative limit throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-088; wave decision: Body ownership]
With limit `10`, reading a 10-byte source returns all 10 bytes and end of stream without error. [D-088]

With limit `10`, reading an 11-byte source without a declared `Content-Length` (a chunked-style source of unknown length) throws the internal over-limit `IOException` subclass (a type distinct from plain `IOException`, named by the implementer) on the read that would return byte 11, and no byte beyond the limit is returned. [D-088] Decision: the over-limit type is `BodyTooLargeException`, and the stream reads at most limit+1 bytes from the source. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-12]

With limit `10` and a declared `Content-Length` of `11`, the first read throws the same internal over-limit `IOException` subclass without reading any byte from the source, so the waves that add body readers can tell it from a transport `IOException` and answer `413`. [D-088] Decision: the exception is `BodyTooLargeException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-13]

records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. This order applies to requests that passed the lifecycle gate; the unrecognised-method-token `501` comes after the validator check and before a `Request` is built.

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`) without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: a pre-request `400` or `501` carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and the `Content-Length` of the standard body; for a `HEAD` method token the `Content-Length` is kept and no body bytes are written. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-14]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them; a recording global middleware, a recording `onError` and a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` record that they were never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
In every handler and middleware call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; I-014]
The HTTP-level assertions of T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 run as tests through the in-memory adapter and the harness in `./gradlew build`. [D-397]

records.requirement: The system shall provide a dispatcher that takes each exchange from an `HttpAdapter` that passed the lifecycle gate of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013, checks the asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` first, then rejects a raw path not starting with `/` with `400`, then rejects a raw path refused by the wave 2 path validator with `400`, and only then calls the router lookup and either runs the middleware pipeline and the matched `RouteHandler` with a `Request` and a `Response` or writes the automatic response, where the pre-request rejections are answered before any `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them, and the two `400` rejections carry the standard error body.

records.title: Automatic responses for router lookup results with the standard error body (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `NOT_FOUND`). [D-395; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: the fallback answers only a response that is still `NEW`, through the request's `Response`, keeping the headers a middleware set; a response that is no longer `NEW` is left as it is. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-15]

With only `POST /p` registered, `GET /p` is answered `405` with `Allow` listing `POST, OPTIONS`, and with `GET /r` registered `DELETE /r` is answered `405` with `Allow` including the automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, both with the standard error body (`code` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`). [D-395; T02; D-134] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order.

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

`TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and `CONNECT /` with `CONNECT` disabled are each answered `501` with the standard error body (`code` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) after the global middleware ran, while a request with an unrecognised method token (FR-ROUTE-013) is answered `501` with the standard error body before any `Request` is built, as FR-HTTP-021 AC-4 states. [D-395; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; D-422] Decision: the dispatcher tells the two cases apart by whether the method token parses to a `Method` value.

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and the standard error body (`code` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`), asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd; wave decision: 426 and 501] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `.

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered with the same `426`, both headers and the standard error body, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and the standard error body. [D-395; T02]

A recording global middleware runs once before each of the `404`, `405`, `426`, automatic `OPTIONS` and disabled-`TRACE`/`CONNECT` `501` answers above and not for the unrecognised-token `501`, and a recording `onError` records no call for any of them. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; residual: onError scope; D-117]

records.requirement: The system shall, after the global and prefix middleware ran, answer the no-match result with `404`, the method-mismatch result with `405` and an `Allow` header, the automatic-OPTIONS result with `204` and an `Allow` header, the unsupported-method result for a disabled `TRACE` or `CONNECT` (a `Method` value) with `501` and the WebSocket-only result with `426` plus `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade`, where the `404`, `405`, `426` and `501` answers carry the standard error body and the `204` answers carry no body, while an unrecognised method token stays a pre-request rejection answered `501` before any `Request` is built (FR-HTTP-021).

records.title: Asterisk-form OPTIONS and raw paths not starting with a slash (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the in-memory adapter, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` with `Allow` listing exactly the methods of `Method.any()` in `Method` declaration order and no body, even when no route is registered. [D-442; loop D: V1-006/V2-004] Decision: the `OPTIONS *` answer has no `Content-Length` header. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-19]

`OPTIONS *` reaches neither the router lookup nor the path validator: with a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is still answered `204` with the `Allow` of AC-1 (not the validator's `400` for a raw path `*`), and `h` records no call. [D-442; D-052]

A raw path `abc` and a raw path `*` with method `GET` are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) without route lookup, and the access log records one line for each. [D-442; wave-4 carried: standard error body; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
The `OPTIONS *` and non-`/` cases are tested through the in-memory adapter in waves 3 and 4; their TinyHttpd counterparts are not asserted in this requirement. [I-021; wave decision: Adapter halves]

records.title: Handler failure and unfinished-response handling through the wave 4 error path

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `INTERNAL_ERROR`) through the harness when no `onError` is registered. [D-127; D-132; wave-4 carried: interim failure handling replaced]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` and header `X-A: 1` but before commit is answered `500` with the standard error body; the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [D-127; D-132; D-134]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a handler can reach before wave 5) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; D-131; wave decision: abort() after completion]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()`, and a middleware that returns without responding or calling `next.run()`, each yield the status and headers set so far (`202` with `X-A: 1`, and `200` for the middleware case) with an empty body, the response is `COMPLETED`, and the app logger received one `warn` naming the method and path. [D-126] Decision: the finishing behaviour is a `warn` through the app logger followed by `end()`; with the response `STREAMING` the dispatcher runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread and logs no warning.

records.requirement: The system shall answer an exception thrown by a handler or middleware through the error path of FR-APP-005, which gives the standard `500` error body while the response is not committed and no `onError` responded, abort the response when the exception is thrown after commit or while streaming, and, when the chain returns with the response not started and no `next.run()`, log a developer warning through the app logger and finish the response with the status and headers set so far and an empty body without waiting for a timeout.

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400 through the error path (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space.

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave-4 carried: malformed query reaches middleware and onError] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse raise `HttpException` with status `400`; the dispatcher parses the query after the middleware ran and before the handler, so global and prefix middleware run, a middleware that reads `req.query(...)` receives that exception, and it reaches `onError` through the error path of FR-APP-005. The query is parsed after the route middleware ran and before the handler; a request without a matched route gets the fallback answer (`404`, `405`, ...) and its query is parsed only if a middleware reads it.

records.title: req.body media-type, syntax, size, depth, UTF-8 and polymorphism checks

acceptanceCriteria.text: Bodies with `Content-Type` `application/json`, `application/json; charset=utf-8`, `application/problem+json` and `APPLICATION/JSON` are decoded, while `text/plain`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `application/jsonx`, `application/json; charset=iso-8859-1` and a missing `Content-Type` make `req.body(...)` throw `UnsupportedMediaTypeException`, answered `415` with the standard error body (code `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`) without calling the codec. [D-186; T09] Decision: an allowed type is `application/json` or `application/<subtype>+json`, compared case-insensitively, with no `charset` parameter or `charset=utf-8`.

The bodies `{"a":`, `[1,]`, an empty body and a body of only spaces and newlines are each answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`; the empty and whitespace-only bodies never reach the codec, and an `IOException` thrown by `JsonCodec.decode` is turned into `HttpException` `400` with that exception as cause unless AC-9 applies. [D-187; T09; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`] Decision: the core maps a codec `IOException` to `400` and lets an unchecked codec exception reach the error path as `500`.
With the default codec, `{"a":1} x` and `{} {}` are answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`. [residual: Trailing JSON data; D-187; T09]

A body of 1048577 bytes with `Content-Length` is answered `413` with code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before the codec reads it, and a chunked body without `Content-Length` larger than the limit, decoded through the default `GsonJsonCodec`, is answered `413` (not `400`) after at most limit + 1 bytes were taken from the exchange stream; with `app.jsonLimit(10)` an 11-byte body gives `413` and a 10-byte body is decoded. [D-188; D-088; T09]
With the default codec, an array nested 65 levels deep is answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST` and one nested 64 levels deep is decoded. [D-189; T09]

A body holding the bytes `{"a":"` `0xC3 0x28` `"}` or a truncated UTF-8 sequence is answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`, because the core decodes the body with a UTF-8 decoder whose malformed and unmappable actions are `REPORT`. [D-190]

Decoding `{"@class":"<canary class>","class":"<canary class>","@type":"<canary class>"}` into `Object.class` with the default codec returns a `Map` and never initialises the canary class, whose static initializer records any loading. [D-191]
The bodies `null` and ` null ` decoded with `req.body(User.class)` and with `req.body(new TypeRef<List<User>>() {})` return `null`. [D-431; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`]

When decoding fails and the core's size-limited stream recorded an overrun (its internal `BodyTooLargeException`, an `IOException` that a codec such as Gson may wrap), the core answers `HttpException` `413`; when the failure's cause chain holds an `HttpException` (for example the adapter `408` of FR-ENGINE-005), that exception is rethrown with its own status; each failure of this requirement reaches `onError` and the access log like any handler exception of FR-APP-005. [D-186; D-187; D-188; D-219] Decision: the overrun is detected from the limited stream's state, not only from the exception the codec rethrows.

records.requirement: The system shall make `req.body(Class)` and `req.body(TypeRef)` accept only `application/json` and `application/*+json` bodies, read them as UTF-8 through the core's size-limited stream and the app codec, and raise `HttpException` with status `415` for another media type, `413` for a body over the JSON limit, and `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST` for an empty, syntactically invalid, too deeply nested, trailing-data or invalid-UTF-8 body, returning `null` for a JSON `null` body and never instantiating a class named inside the input.
records.rationale: Covers D-186, D-187, D-188, D-189, D-190, D-191 and D-431 with the wave decision "A JSON `null` decodes to `null`" (empty body is `400`, not `null`) and the residual "Trailing JSON data" (T09 cases `{"a":1} x` and `{} {}`). Measured fact: Gson 2.14 returns `null` for empty input, so the core must detect an empty or whitespace-only body before calling the codec. Pitfall: an `IOException` from the codec means malformed input (`400`), but an `HttpException` thrown by the body stream (size `413`, adapter `408`) must pass through with its own status.

records.title: res.json encodes through the app codec and round-trips JSON values

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.json(value)` calls the app codec's `encode` once and sends status 200 (or the status set before) with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a `Content-Length` equal to the encoded byte count. [D-193]

A T08 echo route `res.json(req.body(type))` returns values equal to the sent ones for a POJO `User`, a `List<User>` read through `TypeRef`, the string `"x"`, the numbers `42` and `1.5`, `true` and `null`, while `{"n":42}` read with `req.body(Map.class)` comes back as JSON equal to `{"n":42.0}`, which the test compares as JSON values. [D-194; T08]
`res.json("hello")` sends exactly the 7 bytes `"hello"` and `res.json(null)` sends exactly `null`. [D-195]

A codec whose `encode` writes part of the output and then throws leaves the response uncommitted, and the request is answered `500` with exactly the standard error body of FR-APP-006 and no byte of the partial output. [D-136; D-112; wave-4 carried: res.json serialisation failure]

`res.json(value)` on a response that is already committed or completed throws `IllegalStateException` before calling the codec; on a committed but not completed response (committed in the test through the internal response, as the wave 4 error-path tests do) the error path of FR-APP-005 aborts it, so the client sees an abnormally closed response and no standard error body, and on a completed response the client response stays as completed and nothing more is written. [D-136; FR-APP-005; FR-HTTP-016; wave-4 carried: a committed response is aborted]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `res.json(mapOf("success" to true))` inside a route lambda. [D-193; C-03; I-010]

traceLinks.notes: serialisation failures follow the unified error path

records.requirement: The system shall make `res.json(value)` encode `value` through the app codec into a buffer and then send it with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a matching `Content-Length`, so that POJOs, `List<User>`, strings, numbers, booleans and `null` round-trip unchanged through `req.body` and `res.json` and an encoding failure is handled before the response commits.
records.rationale: Covers D-193, D-194, D-195 and the wave 4 carried case of D-136 and D-112 (`carried-into-wave-5.md`). Encoding into a buffer first means a serialisation exception always happens while the response is uncommitted, so the standard error response of FR-APP-006 replaces it and no partial JSON reaches the client; the committed case is a `res.json` call on a response that is already committed, which the error path of FR-APP-005 handles by the response state. Measured fact recorded in `docs/api/request.md`: the default Gson decodes untyped numbers as `Double`, so an untyped `Map` round-trips to JSON-value equality only.

records.title: GsonJsonCodec with STRICT, Unsafe-free defaults, a nesting limit and end-of-document check

acceptanceCriteria.text: `GsonJsonCodec` is public, final and implements `JsonCodec` with the public constructors `GsonJsonCodec()`, `GsonJsonCodec(Gson)` and `GsonJsonCodec(Gson, int maxDepth)` and the public static method `Gson defaultGson()`; a `null` `Gson` throws `NullPointerException` and a `maxDepth` below 1 or above 255 throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-196; wave decision: The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec] Decision: the depth setting is the constructor argument `maxDepth`, and `GsonJsonCodec()` uses `defaultGson()`.

`defaultGson()` returns a `Gson` built with `Strictness.STRICT` and `disableJdkUnsafe()`: decoding `{a:1}`, `{'a':1}` and `{"a":1 /* c */}` with `new GsonJsonCodec()` throws `IOException`, and through `req.body` each is answered `400`. [D-197; D-198]

Decoding `{}` with `new GsonJsonCodec()` into a class whose only constructor takes arguments throws an unchecked exception and creates no instance, and through `req.body` the request is answered `500`. [D-199] Decision: a codec failure that is not malformed input stays unchecked and gives `500`, because it is a server-side type error.

`new GsonJsonCodec()` and `new GsonJsonCodec(customGson)` both reject an array nested 65 levels deep with `IOException` and decode one nested 64 levels; `new GsonJsonCodec(gson, 10)` rejects 11 levels and decodes 10. [D-189; wave decision: The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec]
`decode` of `{"a":1} x` and of `{} {}` throws `IOException`, while `decode` of `null` and of ` null ` returns `null`. [residual: Trailing JSON data; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`]

Every malformed-input failure of `decode` (syntax, lenient construct, nesting, trailing data, wrong JSON type for the target) is thrown as `java.io.IOException` with the Gson exception as cause, and no `com.google.gson` type appears in a `GsonJsonCodec` method signature other than the constructor and `defaultGson()`. [D-187; D-196]
`encode(null, w)` writes `null`, `encode("hello", w)` writes `"hello"` and `encode` of a `List<User>` writes a JSON array through the configured `Gson`. [D-193; D-195]

`NaruServe-gson` main classes pass the animal-sniffer API 21 check and reference no TinyHttpd type, and a Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.jsonCodec(GsonJsonCodec(GsonJsonCodec.defaultGson(), 32))`. [C-02; I-001; C-03]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-gson` the public final class `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` implementing `JsonCodec`, built with a default `Gson` configured with `Strictness.STRICT` and `disableJdkUnsafe()` or with a caller-built `Gson`, that decodes through a `JsonReader` with a nesting limit of 64 by default for every instance, requires the end of the document after the value, returns `null` for a JSON `null` document and reports malformed input as `IOException`.
records.rationale: Covers D-196, D-197, D-198, D-199, the wave decision "The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec" and the residual "Trailing JSON data". Pitfalls: `Gson.fromJson(JsonReader, Type)` does not check for trailing input, so the codec must check `reader.peek() == END_DOCUMENT`; a caller-built `Gson` must not silently raise the nesting limit to Gson's 255; Gson's `JsonSyntaxException` is unchecked, so the codec converts malformed-input failures to `IOException` for the core's `400` mapping. Rejected alternative: a depth parameter on `JsonCodec.decode` (changes the frozen SPI signature of D-182).

records.title: Explicit entry point RestApp.builder() and the JsonCodec SPI

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(a).jsonCodec(c).build()` returns a `RestApp` whose `state()` is `NEW` and whose class is the internal `DefaultRestApp`; two `build()` calls on one builder return two distinct apps. [D-111; wave-4 carried: public entry point constructs DefaultRestApp] Decision: the entry point is `RestApp.builder()` returning `RestApp.Builder`, a public final nested class whose setters return the builder. Decision: two `build()` calls on one builder share the configured adapter, codec and logger. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-1]

`build()` without `httpAdapter(...)` and `build()` without `jsonCodec(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the missing setter, and `httpAdapter(null)`, `jsonCodec(null)` and `logger(null)` each throw `NullPointerException`. [D-111; D-137] Decision: the adapter is checked first, so a builder missing both names `httpAdapter(...)`, and a `null` setter argument throws at the setter, not at `build()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-2]

An app built without `logger(...)` has `app.logger()` returning an instance of the public console logger `com.snoworca.naruserve.ConsoleLogger` of IR-APP-006, and an app built with `logger(l)` has `app.logger()` returning `l`. [D-169; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: each `build()` without `logger(...)` creates its own new `ConsoleLogger`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-3]

Reflection on `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.JsonCodec` finds exactly the two abstract methods `<T> T decode(java.io.Reader, java.lang.reflect.Type) throws java.io.IOException` and `void encode(java.lang.Object, java.io.Writer) throws java.io.IOException`, and no parameter, return or exception type of the interface lies in a `com.google.gson` package. [D-182; D-112]

`JsonCodec` and `RestApp.Builder` carry nullability annotations on every public parameter and return value, and a Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(adapter).jsonCodec(codec).build()` with a Kotlin object implementing `JsonCodec`. [D-111; D-182; C-03] Decision: package `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` is `@NullMarked` and the `value` parameter of `JsonCodec#encode` is `@Nullable`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Middleware and Next interfaces and the middleware registration methods

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `Middleware` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Request, Response, Next) throws Exception`, and `Next` with exactly the abstract methods `void run()` and `void error(Throwable)`; a Java lambda `(req, res, next) -> next.run()` compiles as a `Middleware`. [D-115; D-116]

`RestApp` declares `use(Middleware)`, `use(String, Middleware)`, the seven overloads `get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options(String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(Method, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(MethodSet, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)`, each returning `RestApp`, and every wave 3 `RestApp` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-005 AC-5 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed to the wave 4 method set: the wave 3 methods plus those of IR-APP-002, IR-APP-003, IR-APP-005, IR-APP-006 and IR-APP-007, with `create()` and `builder()` as the only static methods. [D-119; I-014; D-137] Decision: the route-middleware overloads return `RestApp` like the plain registration methods.

`RouteBuilder` declares `use(Middleware)` returning `RouteBuilder`; middleware added through it applies as route middleware to every method the same builder registers after the `use` call, in `use` call order, so `app.route("/a").use(m1).use(m2).get(h)` runs `m1`, `m2`, then `h` for `GET /a`. [D-137; D-120] Decision: `RouteBuilder.use(middleware)` is adopted and is the way to attach several route middleware; no varargs or multi-middleware overload is added to `RestApp`.

`use(null)`, `use("/api", null)`, `use(null, mw)` and every route-middleware overload with a `null` middleware or handler throw `NullPointerException`, and `use(prefix, mw)` with a prefix that does not start with `/` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-118; D-119] Decision: each refused call throws before anything is recorded. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-7]

No public type of `NaruServe-api` declares a method that resumes a middleware chain from another thread or returns a future, and `Next` has no method other than `run()` and `error(Throwable)`. [D-128]

A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `app.use { req, res, next -> next.run() }`, `app.use("/api") { req, res, next -> next.run() }` and `app.get("/x", mw) { req, res -> res.send("x") }` without a DSL. [D-115; C-03]

records.title: onError, ErrorHandler and the framework HTTP error types

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `ErrorHandler` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Throwable, Request, Response) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onError(ErrorHandler)` returning `RestApp`; `app.onError((error, req, res) -> res.status(500).send("x"))` compiles in Java and `app.onError { error, req, res -> }` in a Kotlin test. [D-129; D-137] Decision: the callback interface is `ErrorHandler` and it may throw `Exception`.

`HttpException` extends `RuntimeException`, has public constructors `(int status)`, `(int status, String message)` and `(int status, String message, Throwable cause)`, and `status()` returns the given status; a status outside `400..599` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-130; D-134] Decision: framework errors expose their status through `HttpException#status()`. Decision: the `IllegalArgumentException` message names the refused status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-9]
`HttpException#code()` returns the `code` value of FR-APP-006 for its status (for example `BAD_REQUEST` for `400`, `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` for `422`). [D-130; D-137]
`new UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` and `new UnsupportedMediaTypeException("m")` are `HttpException`s with `status()` `415` and `code()` `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`. [D-134; wave decision: 415]
`onError(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, and `onError` is a registration method under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002. [D-114; D-129]

records.title: ServiceRegistry, ApplicationContext and the request service accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `ServiceRegistry` exactly `register(Class, Object)`, `registerExternal(Class, Object)`, `get(Class)`, `getOrNull(Class)` and `contains(Class)` with the generic signatures of the requirement, and on `ApplicationContext` (a subinterface of `ServiceRegistry`) `attribute(String, Object)`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `own(AutoCloseable)` and `logger()`. [D-138; D-151] Decision: an externally owned object is registered with `registerExternal(Class<T>, T)`, which the framework never closes.

`get(type)` for a type that is not registered throws `ServiceNotFoundException` (a `RuntimeException`) whose message names the type, and `getOrNull(type)` returns `null` and `contains(type)` returns `false` for it. [D-138] Decision: the `ServiceNotFoundException` message contains the binary name of the type. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-1]

`Request` declares `ApplicationContext application()` and `<T> T service(Class<T> type)`, and every wave 3 `Request` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-001 AC-3 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed so that `service` and `application` are expected on `Request` from wave 4. [D-142; I-014]

`register`, `registerExternal` and `own` with a `null` argument, `get`, `getOrNull` and `contains` with a `null` type, and `attribute` with a `null` key throw `NullPointerException`; the value parameter of `attribute(String, Object)` is `@Nullable` and storing a typed `null` variable (`Object v = null; ctx.attribute(key, v)`) removes the key, because a literal `null` resolves to the read overload; `attribute(key, type)` throws `ClassCastException` when the stored value is not an instance of `type`, as the request attribute store of FR-HTTP-012 does. [D-138; D-144]

The new types carry nullability annotations on public signatures (`getOrNull` and `attribute(String, Class)` `@Nullable`, `get` and `service` `@NonNull`), and a Kotlin test compiles `ctx.register(UserService::class.java, s)` and `req.service(UserService::class.java)` with a non-null result type. [D-138; C-03] Decision: of these signatures only the returns of `getOrNull` and `attribute(String, Class)` are `@Nullable`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Lifecycle API: AppState, onStart/onStop, listen, ServerHandle and shutdown

acceptanceCriteria.text: `AppState.values()` is exactly `NEW, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, FAILED, TERMINATED` in that order, and `app.state()` of a newly built app is `NEW`. [D-152]

Reflection finds `LifecycleCallback` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(ApplicationContext) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onStart(LifecycleCallback)` and `RestApp.onStop(LifecycleCallback)` returning `RestApp`; `onStart(null)` and `onStop(null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-137] Decision: `onStart` and `onStop` share the callback interface `LifecycleCallback`, which may throw `Exception`.

`ServerHandle` declares exactly `int port()`, `String address()` and `AppState state()`; after `listen(0)` succeeded `port()` returns the adapter's `boundPort()`, `address()` returns `127.0.0.1` and `state()` returns the app's current state, so it reads `TERMINATED` after shutdown. [D-155] Decision: the accessors are `port()`, `address()` and `state()`, and `listen` binds to `127.0.0.1`.

`listen(port)` with a port outside `0..65535` throws `IllegalArgumentException` and leaves the state `NEW`; `shutdown(timeout, unit)` with a negative timeout throws `IllegalArgumentException` and with a `null` unit `NullPointerException`. [D-153; D-161] Decision: the argument checks of `listen` and `shutdown` run before any state change. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-6]

`AppStartException` extends `RuntimeException`; it is the type `listen()` throws for a checked start-failure cause (as its cause) and for a start ended by a pending stop. [D-159; D-426] Decision: the unchecked wrapper type is `AppStartException`. Decision: `AppStartException` has a public `(String message, Throwable cause)` constructor. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-7]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.onStart { ctx -> ctx.attribute("k", 1) }`, `val h = app.listen(0)`, `h.port()`, `app.state()` and `app.shutdown(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`. [D-152; D-155; C-03]

records.title: Logger SPI, LogLevel, the console logger and app.logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `Logger` exactly the six abstract methods `trace(String)`, `debug(String)`, `info(String)`, `warn(String)`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)`, and `LogLevel.values()` is `TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR`. [D-168; wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`new ConsoleLogger()` writes `info`, `warn` and `error` records and drops `trace` and `debug`; `new ConsoleLogger(LogLevel.TRACE)` writes all five levels. Each record is one line `<timestamp> <LEVEL> <message>` where the timestamp is formatted with `SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ")` (offset like `+0900`; no `java.time`, no `X` pattern, both absent from Android API 21), checked by a test under two time zones, `TRACE`/`DEBUG`/`INFO` go to `System.out` and `WARN`/`ERROR` to `System.err`, and `error(m, t)` writes the stack trace of `t` after the line. [D-169; D-181] Decision: the console logger defaults to threshold `INFO` and uses this line format. Decision: the console logger reads `System.out` and `System.err` at write time, so a stream replaced through `System.setOut` or `System.setErr` receives later records. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-9]
`ConsoleLogger#close()` and `flush()` flush both streams and leave `System.out` and `System.err` open, so a later `System.out.println` still prints. [wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`app.logger(l)` makes `app.logger()` return `l`, `app.logger()` before any call returns the builder's logger (the console logger by default), and `app.logger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; `logger(l)` is under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 while `logger()` is readable in every state. [D-170; D-114]
`ConsoleLogger` is in `NaruServe-api` and references no SLF4J or `android.*` type. [D-169; D-178]

records.title: Cookie value class and SameSite enum

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie` public and final with exactly one public constructor `(String, String)`, a `getName()` method and no `setName` method; `new Cookie("sid", "abc").getName()` returns `sid` and `getValue()` returns `abc`; `new Cookie(null, "v")` and `new Cookie("n", null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-200]

`Cookie` declares `String getValue()`/`void setValue(String)`, `@Nullable String getPath()`/`void setPath(@Nullable String)`, `@Nullable String getDomain()`/`void setDomain(@Nullable String)`, `int getMaxAge()`/`void setMaxAge(int)`, `boolean getSecure()`/`void setSecure(boolean)`, `boolean isHttpOnly()`/`void setHttpOnly(boolean)` and `@Nullable SameSite getSameSite()`/`void setSameSite(@Nullable SameSite)`; a new cookie has path, domain and SameSite `null`, `getSecure()` and `isHttpOnly()` `false` and `getMaxAge()` `-1`. [D-201; D-208] Decision: setters return `void` like the Servlet `Cookie`, and an unset path, domain or SameSite is `null`.
`SameSite.values()` is exactly `STRICT, LAX, NONE` in that order. [D-202]

`setMaxAge(int)` accepts every `int`: a negative value (the default `-1`) means the attribute is not set, so the cookie is a session cookie, `0` means delete and a positive value is a lifetime in seconds. [D-208] Decision: the default `maxAge` is `-1`, and every negative value means "no `Max-Age`" as in the Servlet `Cookie`.

The constructor rejects with `IllegalArgumentException` a name that is empty or not an RFC 7230 token (for example containing a space, `=`, `;`, `,`, CR or LF), and the constructor and `setValue` reject a value with any character outside RFC 6265 `cookie-octet` (CR, LF, `;`, `,`, space, `\\`, a control character or non-ASCII), except that one pair of surrounding double quotes is accepted; `setPath` and `setDomain` reject CR, LF, `;` and every control character; the exception message names the rejected attribute. [D-205; I-017] Decision: an empty value is allowed, so `new Cookie("sid", "")` is valid.

`Cookie` has a package-private static factory method that builds a cookie from a name and a value without validation; the request-cookie parser in `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` reaches it through the internal class `CookieFactoryHook`, whose `private static final java.lang.reflect.Method` field is resolved once with `Class.forName("com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie")` (which also initialises `Cookie`) and `setAccessible(true)`, so no mutable static field exists and the no-mutable-static check of FR-APP-002 AC-2 still passes; the `NaruServe-api` consumer rules of IR-JSON-001 AC-3 also keep that factory method by name; reflection finds no public or protected member of `Cookie` other than those of AC-1 and AC-2 and the `Object` methods. [residual: Building request cookies; wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; FR-APP-002] Decision: the bridge is a reflective, immutable `Method` handle in `internal.CookieFactoryHook`, with no `java.util.function` type (absent from API 21).

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `val c = Cookie("sid", "v"); c.maxAge = 60; c.secure = true; c.isHttpOnly = true; c.sameSite = SameSite.LAX; c.path = "/"; val p: String? = c.path; val n: String = c.name`. [D-201; C-03; I-010]

records.title: Server settings API: app.server(Configurer<ServerOptions>) and app.trustProxy

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `RestApp server(Configurer<ServerOptions>)` and `RestApp trustProxy(boolean)`; `server(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, both methods throw `IllegalStateException` outside `NEW` through the guard of FR-APP-002, and several `server(...)` calls apply in call order to one options object. [D-225; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter] Decision: the settings entry point is `app.server(options -> ...)` and proxy trust is `app.trustProxy(boolean)` (Express `app.set('trust proxy', true)`).

`ServerOptions` declares exactly these setters, each returning `ServerOptions`, with these defaults and inclusive ranges: `bindAddress(String)` `127.0.0.1`; `allowedHosts(String...)` none; `maxHeaderSize(int bytes)` 16384, 1..1048576; `maxHeaderCount(int)` 100, 1..10000; `maxRequestLineLength(int bytes)` 8190, 1..65534; `headerTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 10 s, `bodyReadTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 30 s and `writeTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 30 s, each 1 ms..1 h; `minBodyRate(int bytesPerSecond)` 240, 1..104857600; `maxWorkers(int)` 64, 1..1024; `maxSseStreams(int)` 128, 1..1024; `maxConnections(int)` 512, 1..65536; `maxUpgradedConnections(int)` 128, 1..65536; `maxConnectionsPerAddress(int)` 256, 1..65536. [D-225; D-215; D-216; D-404; D-413; D-414; residual: Upper bounds on size settings] Decision: these names and maxima; `maxWorkers` is the HTTP worker budget of D-404, and `writeTimeout` maps TinyHttpd's socket write timeout (default 30000 ms) so the socket write timeout that `docs/api/defaults.md` names is configurable.

A value below the minimum or above the maximum of AC-2 makes its setter throw `IllegalArgumentException` naming the setting and the allowed range, and `bindAddress(null)`, `bindAddress("")`, `allowedHosts((String[]) null)`, a `null` or empty host name and a `null` `TimeUnit` throw `NullPointerException` or `IllegalArgumentException`; no setter accepts `0`, a negative value or another value meaning unlimited. [residual: Upper bounds on size settings; I-012]

`maxHeaderSize` changes only the total header size of D-215 and leaves the per-line header limit of D-437 unchanged, and `maxRequestLineLength(n)` is the request-line limit that D-414 turns into TinyHttpd's `inputBufferBytes = max(8192, n + 2)`. [D-437; D-414]
`listen(port)` keeps the loopback default: an app that never calls `server(...)` binds `127.0.0.1`. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; D-211]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.server { o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0").allowedHosts("myphone.local").maxHeaderSize(32768) }` and `app.trustProxy(true)`. [D-225; C-03; I-010]

The `RestApp` surface test of IR-APP-002 AC-2 (`HttpApiSurfaceTest`, the wave 4 method set) is re-pointed to the wave 5 set: the wave 4 methods plus `server`, `trustProxy`, `jsonCodec` and `jsonLimit`, every wave 4 signature unchanged, `create()` and `builder()` still the only static methods and no `@Nullable` position on `RestApp`. [I-014; D-225; D-185]

records.title: HttpAdapter settings bind: ServerSettings value, ErrorRenderer and safe logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: `HttpAdapter` keeps `void bind(String, int, ExchangeHandler) throws IOException` unchanged and gains the `default` method `void bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler) throws IOException` whose body calls `bind(settings.bindAddress(), settings.port(), handler)`; the test-fixtures `InMemoryHttpAdapter` and a minimal adapter that implements only the four wave 3 methods compile and bind unchanged. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; I-014; D-107]

`DefaultRestApp.listen(port)` calls `bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` exactly once with a settings value whose `port()` is the `listen` argument and whose other values equal the frozen `ServerOptions` (defaults when `server(...)` was never called), so a recording adapter sees `127.0.0.1` by default and `0.0.0.0` after `server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0"))`. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; D-225]

`ServerSettings` is a public final class with a getter for every setting of IR-ENGINE-001 AC-2, the port, `Logger logger()` and `ErrorRenderer errorRenderer()`; it has no setter, `allowedHosts()` returns an unmodifiable list, and no parameter, return or field type of `ServerSettings` or `ErrorRenderer` lies outside `java.*` and `com.snoworca.naruserve` packages. [D-104; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter]

The `logger()` of the settings value is the core's exception-safe wrapper of the app logger, so a test app logger that throws on every call, used by an adapter through `settings.logger().warn(...)`, never lets an exception reach the adapter. [wave decision: The adapter gets the safe logger; D-220]

`ErrorRenderer` is a `@FunctionalInterface` with `String render(int status)`; the renderer in the settings returns the standard error body of FR-APP-006 for that status with the `code` of its status and a fresh 16-hex-digit request id on every call, identical in format to the body the dispatcher writes. [D-405; D-132; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter] Decision: the renderer returns the JSON text, which the adapter sends as `application/json; charset=UTF-8`.

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI exchange data contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: The SPI exposes, per request, the request line as the method token, the raw request-target path, the raw query string (or its absence) and the HTTP version, plus the header names and values in received order, a body `InputStream`, the remote address and the secure flag. [D-105] Decision: the headers are exposed as a `List<Map.Entry<String, String>>` in received order with duplicates kept, not as a `Map`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-1]

The SPI accepts from the core a status code, response headers and a body `OutputStream`, and the core writes status and headers before the first body byte. [D-105] Decision: status, headers and the content length (`-1` when unknown) pass in one `commit` call that returns the body `OutputStream`, and a second start of the response throws `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-2] The exchange outlives `ExchangeHandler#handle` until the core calls `finish` or `abort`, and the adapter may force-close it only at its stop deadline; `abort()` is idempotent and thread-safe (it may run on any thread, also while another thread is in `commit`, a body write or `finish`, which then fail with an `IOException`). The headers passed to `commit` are sent as given: they already carry `Content-Length` when the core knows it (a `HEAD` response carries the length the `GET` body would have had) and the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`; `contentLength` is the number of body bytes the core will write, `0` for a bodyless response (`204`, `304`, `HEAD`) or `-1` when unknown, which the adapter frames itself (chunked, or close on HTTP/1.0) and is the only case where it may add a framing header. Header names and values are ISO-8859-1: the core guarantees every char is at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, so the adapter writes each char as one byte. [wave 3 implementation decision]

The raw request-target path and the raw query string travel through the SPI as separate undecoded fields: an exchange with target `/a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and the core alone yields `req.path()` = `/a b` and `req.query("x")` = `A`. [D-399; wave decision: Adapter halves] Decision: the raw query is `null` when the target has no `?`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-3]

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI extension points and bind/stop lifecycle

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the file-transfer extension point the core hands the adapter a `java.io.File` with an offset and a length, and the adapter writes exactly those bytes of the file as the response body; an in-memory test hands over a file with a non-zero offset and a length shorter than the rest of the file and reads back exactly that byte range from the client body. [D-106]

Through the protocol-upgrade extension point the core hands the adapter an upgrade callback with a `101` response, and the adapter invokes that callback with the exchange's raw input and output streams after writing the `101` response; an in-memory test observes that the callback ran with the exchange's streams (or that the in-memory adapter recorded the hand-over). [D-106]

The event-stream point hands the adapter a core-owned drain loop that keeps writing after the handler returned until the core reports the stream ended, and the adapter chooses the thread that runs it; in wave 3 (before `res.sse` exists) an in-memory test supplies a drain loop through the SPI type, runs it on an adapter-chosen thread after the handler returned and sees it end only when the end is reported. [D-106] Decision: `eventStream` returns to the caller at once, and the in-memory adapter runs the drain on its own worker thread, completing the client response when the drain returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-4]

The three extension points are SPI types in `NaruServe-api`, usable by an adapter without any NaruServe class outside `NaruServe-api`, so waves 6, 7 and 8 add adapter classes against them without changing the SPI. [D-106]

The SPI declares a bind to an address and port that returns only after binding completed, and a separate call through which the core reads the actual bound port; with the in-memory adapter, a bind with port `0` reports a positive bound port that the core reads back through the SPI and that stays the same on every read until stop, and a bind with a positive port reports that port. [D-107] Decision: for a bind with port `0` the in-memory adapter assigns a positive port from a counter starting at `49152`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-5]

The SPI declares a blocking stop that stops accepting, waits for in-flight exchanges until a deadline passed by the core and then force-closes the remaining connections, and a separate final release that waits at most a fixed margin for the adapter's threads to end; the in-memory adapter implements both and a test shows an in-flight exchange still running at the deadline is force-closed. [D-107] Decision: an exchange in flight at the deadline is aborted so its client response reports `abnormallyClosed`, and the in-memory adapter's release shuts its worker pool waiting at most 1 second. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: TypeRef captures generic types and ships consumer R8/ProGuard rules

acceptanceCriteria.text: `new TypeRef<List<User>>() {}.getType()` returns a `ParameterizedType` whose raw type is `java.util.List` and whose only argument is `User`, and `new TypeRef<String>() {}.getType()` returns `String.class`. Constructing a raw subclass (`new TypeRef() {}`) or a subclass whose type argument is a type variable (inside `<X> TypeRef<X> make() { return new TypeRef<X>() {}; }`) throws `IllegalStateException` whose message says that a concrete type argument is required. records.title: Immutable MethodSet combinators

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `MethodSet s = Method.get()`, calling `s.post()` returns a set containing `GET` and `POST`, and `s` still contains only `GET` afterwards; the same holds for every combinator and for `except`. records.title: Lookup result contract and precedence

acceptanceCriteria.text: The result type exposes exactly six kinds and each lookup returns exactly one; the matched kind carries the handler, the path parameters, the actual method (the request method for a direct match, `GET` under automatic `HEAD` and for a WebSocket match; it does not decide the wave 3 `req.method()` value, D-398), the route kind and the automatic-`HEAD` flag, and the method-mismatch and automatic-OPTIONS kinds carry an `Allow` `MethodSet`. [D-390] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-1] A field a kind does not carry reads as null (handler, method, route kind, allow) and params reads as an empty map.

An unrecognised method token yields unsupported method even when no pattern matches the path, and a recognised method on a path no pattern matches yields no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]
On a matched path a route of the request method wins over automatic OPTIONS and automatic `HEAD`, which win over WebSocket-only, which wins over method mismatch. [wave decision: lookup result order]

The lookup takes the raw, undecoded path as received in the request target, so a lookup of `GET /files/%252e` against `GET /files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`; the path is checked with the path validator before any result is chosen, so a rejected path such as `/a%zz` fails with `IllegalArgumentException` for every method token, and "whatever the path" elsewhere in this scope means whatever accepted path. [D-051; loop W residual: validator does not decode] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-2] The `IllegalArgumentException` names the path and is thrown before the method token is read.

The upgrade flag is ignored unless the method token is `GET`; registering a route after the freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, a lookup before a successful freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, and the routing configuration error is an exception type of its own (name decided under C-07), distinct from `IllegalStateException` and `IllegalArgumentException`. [wave decision: route kind; D-058]

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/cookie.md` states that `getMaxAge()` defaults to `-1`, that every negative value omits `Max-Age` (a session cookie), that `0` deletes and that a positive value is seconds, with its reason (the Servlet `Cookie` model), and the `getMaxAge()` row has no (미확정) marker. [D-208; I-013]

`docs/api/cookie.md` states that v1 writes no `Expires` attribute (lifetimes use `Max-Age`) and has no signed cookies (an app signs values itself, for example with an HMAC in middleware), each with its reason, and the `Expires` marker line is gone. [D-208; I-013]

`docs/api/cookie.md` states that NaruServe neither encodes nor decodes cookie values, unlike Express's `res.cookie`, that an app encodes other characters itself (for example with `URLEncoder`), that request cookies with an invalid name or without `=` are skipped instead of failing the request, and that `res.addCookie` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an invalid name or value. [wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; D-205]
The `cookie-parser` row of `docs/api/express-migration.md` states that signed cookies and automatic value encoding are not provided in v1 instead of carrying a (미확정) marker. [D-208]

The Java blocks of `docs/api/cookie.md` are compiled by the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 with no skip entry whose reason is `Cookie`, `req.cookie`, `req.getCookies` or `res.addCookie`, and a docs test fails when `docs/api/cookie.md` contains a (미확정) marker. [I-008; I-009]
