records.title: Wave 5 engine and server-setting decisions recorded in docs/api with defaults checked against the code

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/app.md` documents `app.server(options -> ...)` with every setter of IR-ENGINE-001 AC-2, a LAN example `options.bindAddress("0.0.0.0").allowedHosts("myphone.local")` in Java and Kotlin, `app.trustProxy(true)`, that `ServerHandle.address()` reports the address actually bound (`127.0.0.1` by default), and that one non-daemon keeper thread keeps the JVM alive after `main` returns while TinyHttpd's threads stay daemon; the LAN binding marker line is gone and no sentence says the server threads are non-daemon. [D-225; D-212; D-167; wave decision: Thread wording; wave decision: The default bind address is IPv4 `127.0.0.1`]

`docs/api/defaults.md` lists header size 16 KiB (`431`, `maxHeaderSize`), request-line length 8190 bytes (`414`, `maxRequestLineLength`, renamed from URL length), the per-line header limit of `inputBufferBytes - 2` (8190 by default, `431`, unchanged by `maxHeaderSize`), header count 100, header timeout 10 s, body-read timeout 30 s, write timeout 30 s, minimum body rate 240 B/s (`408`), the connection limits (workers 64, SSE streams 128, connections 512, derived wait queue 320, upgraded connections 128, per address 256) and the maximum of every setting; it states that no setting accepts an unlimited value, drops the sentence that `431`/`414` are not final, and the markers on these rows and on the unlimited-value question are gone. [D-225; D-437; residual: Upper bounds on size settings; I-012]

`docs/api/defaults.md` states that the bind default is `127.0.0.1`, that `bindAddress("0.0.0.0")` always logs a security warning and the app must add authentication itself, names `app.trustProxy(true)` for `X-Forwarded-*`, lists the D-400 transport-level rejections (`400`, `408`, `414`, `417`, `431`, `501`, `505` and the socket-level `503`) as plain-text answers that bypass `onError`, the error JSON and the access log, records the `421` Host rejection with the standard error body, and states that the TinyHttpd adapter has no TLS listener in v1; the binding and proxy markers are gone. [D-213; D-400; D-418; D-433; wave decision: The LAN warning is unconditional]

`docs/api/request.md` names `app.trustProxy(true)` in its proxy paragraph without a marker, and `docs/api/express-migration.md` maps `app.set('trust proxy', ...)` to `app.trustProxy(true)` and names `bindAddress("0.0.0.0")` in its LAN sentence, both without markers. [D-225; D-080]

`docs/api/README.md`, `docs/api/app.md` and `docs/api/json.md` name the bootstrap module `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe` and the Gson module `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe-gson` exactly as CON-BUILD-002 and CON-BUILD-005 fixed them, which a docs test checks. [D-230]

A test parses the defaults of AC-2, the JSON size and depth rows of `docs/api/defaults.md` and compares them with the defaults of `ServerOptions`, `app.jsonLimit` and `GsonJsonCodec`, failing on any difference; the Java blocks that call `server`, `trustProxy` or `ServerOptions` are compiled by the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 with no skip entry naming them. [I-011; I-009]

The other (미확정) markers that these decisions settle are removed in the same change: the sentence of `docs/api/defaults.md` on socket read/write timeouts, header count, wait queue and SSE/WebSocket connection limits names `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `maxHeaderCount`, the derived queue, `maxSseStreams` and `maxUpgradedConnections`; `docs/api/sse.md` names `maxSseStreams` for the concurrent SSE connection limit; the `docs/api/websocket.md` limits row names `maxUpgradedConnections` for the connection count while idle timeout, ping interval and handshake timeout keep their wave 7 marker; and the trust-proxy and LAN-binding bullet leaves the undecided list of `docs/api/express-migration.md`. [D-225; D-404; I-008; I-013]

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/request.md` states that `rawPath()` returns the raw, undecoded path without the query string (available through `req.query(...)`), gives its Express counterpart as `req.path` before decoding (not `req.originalUrl`), and has no (미확정) marker on the `rawPath()` row. `docs/api/app.md` lists `routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` among the `RestApp` methods with a Java and a Kotlin example and adds no (미확정) marker for it. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/defaults.md` names `app.routerPolicy(...)` with `enableTrace`/`enableConnect` as the explicit `TRACE`/`CONNECT` policy, and that row has no (미확정) marker. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/express-migration.md` no longer maps `req.originalUrl` to `req.rawPath()`: the `rawPath()` row names `req.path` before decoding as its Express counterpart without a marker, and a kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query string read through `req.query(...)` or states that it has no direct counterpart, without a marker; the `express.raw()`/`express.text()` marker is replaced with the statement that v1 has no raw or text body reader, and the raw/text bullet is removed from the undecided list (section 'Express에 있지만 아직 정해지지 않은 기능'), so the file states once, without contradiction, that v1 has no raw or text body reader. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Body ownership] Decision: the kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query read through `req.query(...)`. records.title: Wave 3 decisions in docs/api with the later-wave markers kept (wave 5)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/request.md` states that `rawPath()` returns the raw, undecoded path without the query string (available through `req.query(...)`), gives its Express counterpart as `req.path` before decoding (not `req.originalUrl`), and has no (미확정) marker on the `rawPath()` row. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC1

`docs/api/request.md` states that `req.attribute(name, type)` throws `ClassCastException` for a stored value of another type, without a marker, and that a value is removed by storing a typed `null` variable because a literal `null` resolves to the read overload. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Null attribute values] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC2

`docs/api/response.md` states that `send(byte[])` without a `Content-Type` uses `application/octet-stream` and that `stream(InputStream, contentType)` takes ownership and closes the stream on success, failure or abort, with an example that does not use try-with-resources, and the marker line on these two points is gone. [D-109; wave decision: stream() closing; wave decision: Remaining markers] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC3

`docs/api/routing.md` documents `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` with `RouterPolicy.builder()` (`mergeSlashes`, `ignoreTrailingSlash`, `caseInsensitive`, `enableTrace`, `enableConnect`) as allowed only while the app is in `NEW` (before `listen()`), like every setting in `app.md` (a call outside `NEW` is rejected with `IllegalStateException` by the state guard of FR-APP-002), has no sentence calling that name undecided, and states that `req.method()` returns `HEAD` during automatic `HEAD`; its marker set is checked by OPS-ROUTE-003 AC-3. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: req.method() during automatic HEAD; wave-3 residual: marker test of wave 2] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC4

`docs/api/app.md` lists `routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` among the `RestApp` methods with a Java and a Kotlin example and adds no (미확정) marker for it. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC5

`docs/api/defaults.md` names `app.routerPolicy(...)` with `enableTrace`/`enableConnect` as the explicit `TRACE`/`CONNECT` policy, and that row has no (미확정) marker. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC6

`docs/api/express-migration.md` does not map `req.originalUrl` to `req.rawPath()`: the `rawPath()` row names `req.path` before decoding as its Express counterpart without a marker, the kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query read through `req.query(...)` without a marker, and the file states once, without contradiction, that v1 has no raw or text body reader, with no raw/text bullet in the undecided list (section 'Express에 있지만 아직 정해지지 않은 기능'). [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Body ownership] re_stated_from: OPS-HTTP-003#AC7

`HttpDocsTest`, re-pointed to this requirement, checks that the markers of later waves than wave 5 stay — `file` disposition and `redirect` in `response.md`, `parts()` in `request.md` and the markers of `express-migration.md` owned by issues of waves 6 to 8 — that `routing.md` keeps no marker, and that the proxy-trust and `jsonTree()`/`jsonMap()` markers of `request.md` are gone because wave 5 decides them (OPS-ENGINE-001 AC-4, OPS-JSON-001 AC-2). records.title: Wave 5 JSON decisions and nullable req.body examples recorded in docs/api

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/json.md` names `app.jsonLimit(bytes)` (default 1 MiB, at most 1 GiB) and `new GsonJsonCodec(gson, maxDepth)` (default 64, at most 255, kept also for a caller-built `Gson`), states that trailing data after the value and an empty body are answered `400`, and its limit section has no (미확정) marker; the JSON rows of `docs/api/defaults.md` name the same APIs without markers. [D-192; I-013]

`docs/api/request.md` states that `req.body(...)` returns `null` for a JSON `null` body, that `415`, `400` and `413` are its failure statuses, and that v1 has no `jsonTree()`/`jsonMap()` (use `req.body(Map.class)`) with its reason, and the `jsonTree()`/`jsonMap()` marker is gone. [D-192; D-431]

In `docs/api/kotlin.md` the nullability table row `req.body(type)` reads `T?` without a marker, the `val users: List<User>` example and the `val body = req.body(CreateUserRequest::class.java)` example followed by `body.name` use a nullable type with safe-call syntax or the reified extension, and the extension shown reads `inline fun <reified T : Any> Request.body(): T = body(T::class.java) ?: throw HttpException(400, "JSON body is null")` with a sentence on the JSON `null` decision. [D-440; D-192] Decision: the reified extension of D-354 throws `HttpException` `400` for a JSON `null` body.

The `val user = req.body(User::class.java)` example of `docs/api/README.md` and the `val todo = req.body(Todo::class.java)` example of `docs/api/express-migration.md` no longer pass a possibly-null value to a non-null parameter: each uses safe-call or elvis syntax or the reified extension. [D-440]

A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs each rewritten `req.body(...)` example of AC-3 and AC-4 against the wave 5 API, declaring the example types (`User`, `CreateUserRequest`, `Todo`) and, for examples that call `req.body<T>()`, a test-local copy of the extension shown in AC-3 (the module extension of D-354 arrives in wave 8). In the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004, whose fixed import set stays unchanged, every skip entry in any `docs/api` file whose only reason is `res.json`, `req.body`, `TypeRef`, `jsonCodec`, `Cookie`, `req.cookie`, `req.getCookies` or `res.addCookie` is removed when its block now compiles, or re-pointed to the reason that still applies (a Gson type outside the fixed imports, an app-defined type such as `User`, or a later-wave member such as `ws.sendJson`), so the OPS-APP-002 AC-2 rule (a skip entry whose block compiles fails the test) holds. [D-440; D-349; D-351; I-009; OPS-APP-002] Decision: the docs compile test keeps its fixed imports, so Gson-using blocks stay skipped with the Gson reason; the root test classpath may gain `project(':NaruServe-gson')` for the defaults test of OPS-ENGINE-001 AC-6.

records.title: Access log never records secrets and escapes control characters

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request `POST /login?token=qzv&password=pwz` with `Authorization: Bearer s3cr3t`, `Cookie: sid=c00k1e` and body `password=pwq2` whose handler answers `token-xyz` produces a line that contains none of `qzv`, `pwz`, `s3cr3t`, `c00k1e`, `pwq2`, `token-xyz` or `?`. [D-175; T39] Decision: the line is built only from the method token, the raw path without the query, the status, the duration and byte counts and the request id. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-11]

A raw path containing `%0d%0a` is logged with the raw percent-encoded form, and an unrecognised method token or path containing a CR, LF, TAB, `0x01`, `0x7F` or `0x85` character is logged with `\r`, `\n`, `\t` and `\u0001`, `\u007f`, `\u0085`, and `\` as `\\`, so every access log record is one line. [D-176; T39] Decision: control characters U+0000–U+001F, U+007F and U+0080–U+009F are escaped this way. Decision: other escaped characters are written as `\u` plus four lowercase hex digits, and percent-encoded text stays raw. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-12]
The access log line holds no header value at all. [D-175]
